name: Raymond-Roy
description: The Raymond and Roy scale is the most commonly used grading scale to assess aneurysm occlusion after coiling. This grading scale divides the outcomes of treated aneurysms into 3 categories: 1) complete occlusion, 2) residual neck, and 3) residual aneurysm.
description_reference: Rouchaud A, Brinjikji W, Gunderson J, et al. Validity of the Meyer Scale for Assessment of Coiled Aneurysms and Aneurysm Recurrence. American journal of neuroradiology 2016; 37: 844-8. https://doi.org/10.3174/ajnr.A4616
domain_match_overall_rationale: Raymond-Roy is a simple 3 category scale that distinguishes complete aneurysm occlusion from residual neck and residual aneurysm; however, it is primarily used for assessing coiling treatment.
domain_match_1_rationale: Raymond-Roy is a 3 category scale that distinguishes complete aneurysm occlusion from residual neck and residual aneurysm.
domain_match_2_rationale: Assesses aneurysm occlusion after coiling treatment.
domain_match_3_rationale: Classifications reflect the angiographic status of the treated aneurysm.
domain_match_5_rationale: Can be applied after treatment and at follow-up.
domain_match_6_rationale: Provides clinically meaningful differentiation between complete occlusion, neck remnant, and residual aneurysm

name: Modified Raymond–Roy Classification
domain_match_overall_rationale: The Modified Raymond-Roy Classification distinguishes between complete occlusion, neck remnant, and different forms of residual aneurysm; however, it is primarily used for assessing coiling treatment.
domain_match_1_rationale: Expands on the orginal Raymond-Roy scale to distinguishes (1) complete aneurysm occlusion from (2)residual neck and (3)residual aneurysm with (a) flow into the spaces between  coils or (b) along the anuerysm wall.
domain_match_2_rationale: Assesses aneurysm occlusion after coiling treatment.
domain_match_3_rationale: Classifications reflect the angiographic status of the treated aneurysm.
domain_match_4_rationale: Simple, clearly defined categories; improved characterization compared with the original three-category Raymond Roy scale.
domain_match_5_rationale: Can be applied after treatment and at follow-up.
domain_match_6_rationale: Provides clinically meaningful differentiation between complete occlusion, neck remnant, and different forms of residual aneurysm

name: Meyer scale
description: The Meyer scale is a 6-point grading scale based on the percentage of the aneurysm filled by contrast on DSA (digital subtraction angiography). Grade zero indicates complete aneurysm occlusion. Grade 1 represents >90% aneurysm occlusion; grade 2, 70%–89% aneurysm occlusion; grade 3, 50%–69%; grade 4, 25%–49%; and grade 5, <25% volumetric aneurysm occlusion. Two other “modifier” criteria are combined with this scale: The modifier “I” may be used to describe interstitial opacification within the confines of the coil mass and the modifier “G” may be used to describe interval growth in the overall dimensions of the aneurysm as a separate phenomenon from coil compaction with recurrence of the aneurysm.
description_reference: Rouchaud A, Brinjikji W, Gunderson J, et al. Validity of the Meyer Scale for Assessment of Coiled Aneurysms and Aneurysm Recurrence. American journal of neuroradiology 2016; 37: 844-8. https://doi.org/10.3174/ajnr.A4616
domain_match_overall_rationale: Grades the degree to which a treated aneurysm is occluded, from Grade 0 (complete occlusion) to Grade 5 (<25 % occlusion); however, it is mainly applicable to coil treated aneurysms.
domain_match_1_rationale: Grades the degree to which a treated aneurysm is occluded, from Grade 0 (complete occlusion) to Grade 5 (<25 % occlusion).
domain_match_3_rationale: Grades the treated aneurysm based on the % occluded.
domain_match_4_rationale: Grades the treated aneurysm based on the percentage of the aneurysm filled by contrast on DSA (digital subtraction angiography).
domain_match_5_rationale: Can be applied immediately after coiling and at follow-up.
domain_match_6_rationale: Provides percentage-based categories from complete occlusion (Grade 0) to <25% occlusion (Grade 5).

name: Unnamed 3-point occlusion scale
description: Several ordinal scales have been proposed for angiographic follow-up. These scales are either descriptive or use estimates of percent volumetric occlusion. Ordinal scales usually use descriptors such as “complete,” “near-complete,” or “incomplete” occlusion, and some scales use terms such as “neck remnant,” “dog ear,” “residual neck,” and “residual” aneurysm.
description_reference: Suh SH, Cloft HJ, Lanzino K, et al. Interobserver Agreement after Pipeline Embolization Device Implantation. American Journal of Neuroradiology 2013; 34: 1215–18. https://doi.org/10.3174/ajnr.A3371

name: Quantitative percent measures
description:
Percent Embolization: the total percentage of the extent of embolization.

Two-dimensional Percent Occlusion (2DPO): percentage scale that estimates aneurysm occlusion based on two-dimensional imaging.

Volumetric Packing Density (vPD): measures how densely the aneurysm has been packed with coils.
description_reference: Lee JY, Kwon BJ, Cho YD, et al. Reappraisal of anatomic outcome scales of coiled intracranial aneurysms in the prediction of recanalization. Journal of Korean Neurosurgical Society 2013; 53: 342-8. https://doi.org/10.3340/jkns.2013.53.6.342
domain_match_overall_rationale: Quantitative percent measures provide an estimate of how much the aneurysm has been closed off from cerebral circulation; however, 2D estimates can misrepresent true 3D residual volume and clinical interpretation may be needed if there are no validated classification cutoffs.
domain_match_1_rationale: Provides a percentage estimate of how much the aneurysm has been closed off from cerebral circulation.
domain_match_2_rationale: Quantitative percent measures can describe a continuum from no occlusion to 100%; however, 2D percentage cannot describe the 3D structure of the aneurysm. Quantitative percent measures are most often used to describe coiling treatment.
domain_match_3_rationale: 2D estimates can misrepresent true 3D residual volume.
domain_match_4_rationale: The quantitative percent measurements themself should be standard; however, approaches/measurements may differ across studies, and clinical interpretation is needed in the absence of well defined classifications/thresholds.
domain_match_5_rationale: Can be calculated after treatment and at follow-up.
domain_match_6_rationale: Quantitative percent measures provide granularity, but clinical judgement may be needed in the absence of validated cutoffs.

name: Angiographic Grading Scale
description: The Angiographic Grading Scale (AGS) is a categorical occlusion scale, usually determined by visual estimation. The common three-category version (2,3, or 4 category versions exist) includes complete occlusion, residual neck, and residual aneurysms.
description_reference: Lee JY, Kwon BJ, Cho YD, et al. Reappraisal of anatomic outcome scales of coiled intracranial aneurysms in the prediction of recanalization. Journal of Korean Neurosurgical Society 2013; 53: 342-8. https://doi.org/10.3340/jkns.2013.53.6.342
domain_match_overall_rationale: Angiographic Grading Scales appears to be an umbrella term for existing visual estimation occlusion scales, rather than a uniue scale itself. AGS was described as having 2, 3, or 4 category versions, but some of these have the same classifications as other scales on this list of candidate instruments. Pointing directly to these other, original source, scales (e.g., Raymond Roy) may be clearer when recommending an instrument for the COS.
domain_match_1_rationale: Grades whether the aneurysm is completely occluded, has a residual neck, or retains residual aneurysm filling, so it directly addresses whether the aneurysm has been eliminated from circulation.
domain_match_2_rationale: Captures degrees of residual filling, but was developed around coiled aneurysms and does not explicitly accommodate other treatment types.
domain_match_3_rationale: The categories specifically describe residual blood flow within the treated aneurysm.
domain_match_4_rationale: Does not refer to a single grading system.
domain_match_5_rationale: Can be applied immediately after treatment and at follow-up.
domain_match_6_rationale: 2, 3, or 4 category versions exist. Unable to say without a specified version.

name: WEB Occlusion Scale
description: The WEB Occlusion Scale (WOS), based upon the modified Raymond Scale, is an angiographic assessment scale for the standardized reporting of aneurysm occlusion achieved with intrasaccular mesh implants. Grade A and B indicate complete occlusion, with (A) or without (B) visible collection of contrast. Residual neck filling (C) is indicated by contrast opacification of the aneurysm neck. Residual aneurysm filling (D) is indicated by contrast opacification extending beyond the aneurysm neck and into the fundus.
description_reference: Fiorella D, Arthur A, Byrne J, et al. Interobserver variability in the assessment of aneurysm occlusion with the WEB aneurysm embolization system. Journal of NeuroInterventional Surgery 2015; 7: 591-595.
domain_match_overall_rationale: The WEB Occlusion Scale (WOS) is an angiographic assessment scale for the standardized reporting of aneurysm occlusion achieved with intrasaccular mesh implants. Grade A and B indicate complete occlusion, with (A) or without (B) visible collection of contrast; Grade C indicates residual neck filling (C); and Grade D indicates residual aneurysm filling. The primary domain match limitation for WOS is its specificity to WEB treatment.
domain_match_1_rationale: Assesses whether a WEB-treated aneurysm is completely occluded or retains neck/aneurysm filling.
domain_match_3_rationale: Categories reflect residual blood flow into the aneurysm and/or WEB device.
domain_match_4_rationale: Grades distinguish complete occlusion, complete occlusion with recess filling, residual neck, and residual aneurysm.
domain_match_5_rationale: Can be applied at follow-up and identify changes in WEB occlusion over time.
domain_match_6_rationale: Provides clear categorical distinction between complete and incomplete results, with substantial interobserver reliability reported.

name: Bicêtre Occlusion Scale Score
description: The Bicêtre Occlusion Scale Score (BOSS) assesses aneurysm closure after Woven EndoBridge (WEB) treatment. Scores 0 and 0′ indicate complete occlusion, while higher scores indicate increasing residual blood flow in or around the device or aneurysm [0 = no residual flow inside the aneurysm or the WEB; 0’ = opacification of the proximal recess of the WEB; 1 = residual flow inside the WEB; 2 = neck remnant; 3 = aneurysm remnant; and 1 + 3 = contrast agent media depicted inside and around the device].
description_reference: Caroff J, Mihalea C, Tuilier, et al. Occlusion Assessment of Intracranial Aneurysms Treated with the WEB Device. Neuroradiology 2016; 58: 887–91. https://doi.org/10.1007/s00234-016-1715-9
domain_match_overall_rationale: Assesses residual flow following aneurysm treatment, including complete occlusion and patterns of incomplete occlusion; however, it is specific to WEB treatment.
domain_match_1_rationale: Assesses residual flow following WEB treatment, including complete occlusion and patterns of incomplete occlusion.
domain_match_3_rationale: Categories specifically reflect whether and where contrast continues to fill the treated aneurysm/device.
domain_match_4_rationale: BOSS provides explicit categories (0, 0′, 1, 2, 3) based on the observed pattern of residual contrast.
domain_match_5_rationale: Can assess occlusion post-treatment and at follow-up occlusion.
domain_match_6_rationale: Classifies complete occlusion, WEB recess filling, intradevice filling, neck remnant, and aneurysm remnant.

name: Ozpeynirci Scale 4-value occlusion scale
description: The Ozpeynirci Scale is a 4-grade scale used to assess aneurysm occlusion after treatment with the Woven EndoBridge (WEB) device. Grade 1 represents total occlusion, grade 2 represents neck remnant, grade 3a represents contrast enhancement inside the WEB, and grade 3b represents aneurysm remnant.
description_reference: Comby P, Finitsis S, Iancu D, et al. Reliability and Applicability of Angiographic Outcome Scales in WEB Device-Treated Aneurysms: A Systematic Review. Neuroradiology 2025; 67: 191–99. https://doi.org/10.1007/s00234-024-03526-5
domain_match_overall_rationale: The Ozpeynirci Scale is a 4-grade scale used to assess aneurysm occlusion after treatment with the Woven EndoBridge (WEB) device. It's main limitation is specificity to WEB treatment.
domain_match_1_rationale: 4-grade scale used to assess aneurysm occlusion after treatment with the Woven EndoBridge (WEB) device.
domain_match_3_rationale: Categories describe residual filling and whether complete obliteration has occurred
domain_match_4_rationale: The Ozpeynirci Scale uses a clearly defined 4-grade scale.
domain_match_5_rationale: Can be applied during follow-up to determine assesses the WEB-treated aneurysm.
domain_match_6_rationale: Clearly defined grading system: Grade 1 represents total occlusion, grade 2 represents neck remnant, grade 3a represents contrast enhancement inside the WEB, and grade 3b represents aneurysm remnant.

name: Unnamed dichotomized occlusion scale
description:
Dichotomized occlusion scale: Assesses whether there is complete occlusion or not.

2-response occlusion scale: Assessment of angiographic change to describe the treated aneurysm as "not worse" or "worse".
description_reference:
Caroff J, Mihalea C, Tuilier T, et al. Occlusion Assessment of Intracranial Aneurysms Treated with the WEB Device. Neuroradiology 2016; 58: 887–91. https://doi.org/10.1007/s00234-016-1715-9

Cloft HJ, Kaufmann T, Kallmes DF, et al. Observer agreement in the assessment of endovascular aneurysm therapy and aneurysm recurrence. American journal of neuroradiology 2007; 28: 497-500.
domain_match_overall_rationale: The dichotomized occlusion scale assesses whether there is complete occlusion or not. The referenced version was a simplification of the BOSS scale, which is a 5 grade scale that assesses aneurysm closure after Woven EndoBridge (WEB) treatment.
domain_match_1_rationale: Assesses whether there is complete occlusion or not.
domain_match_2_rationale: Used in WEB context; converted from BOSS scale.
domain_match_3_rationale: Classifications reflect complete occlusion or not complete occlusion.
domain_match_4_rationale: A two-category scale is simple, which could improve standadization; however, the lack of a distinct name/reference may cause it to be confused with other dichotomized scales and/or be inconsistently applied. This particular scale was derived from the BOSS scale.
domain_match_5_rationale: Can be applied post-operation and at follow-up.
domain_match_6_rationale: Simple (complete occlusion or not complete occlusion), but compresses the full range of outcomes (5 BOSS grades) into a dichotomous scale that may not represent all clinically relevant outcomes.

name: O’Kelly–Marotta Scale
description: The O’Kelly–Marotta (OKM) scale incorporates 2 dimensions as parameters, which reflect the mechanism by which flow-diverting devices accomplish aneurysm protection: reduction in aneurysm sac filling (filling grade), which reflects an anatomic aspect, and promotion of stasis within the aneurysm sac (stasis grade), which reflects a more dynamic or physiologic parameter.
description_reference: Joshi MD, O'Kelly, CJ, Krings T, et al. Observer variability of an angiographic grading scale used for the assessment of intracranial aneurysms treated with flow-diverting stents. American journal of neuroradiology 2013; 34: 1589-92. https://doi.org/10.3174/ajnr.A3431
domain_match_overall_rationale: The OKM scale was developed specifically for the angiographic assessment of aneurysms treated with flow-diverting stents. Joshi et al. found that the interobserver variability of the OKM grading scale is comparable with well-established angiographic grading schemes for treated aneurysms. In this specific case of FD treated aneurysms, this appears to be a good match, provided that its limited applicability to FD aneurysms is made clear. The lack of ability of this scale to predict aneurysm occlusion at follow-up may hinder its clinical utility (Raper et al 2019.)
domain_match_1_rationale: Evaluates residual aneurysm filling after flow diversion treatment.
domain_match_3_rationale: Incorporates 2 dimensions which reflect the mechanism by which flow-diverting devices accomplish aneurysm protection: reduction in aneurysm sac filling (filling grade), and promotion of stasis within the aneurysm sac (stasis grade).
domain_match_4_rationale: Provides explicit filling grades and stasis grades.
domain_match_5_rationale: Flow diversion produces progressive occlusion, so an early OKM grade may not describe final success or failure.
domain_match_6_rationale: Distinguishes complete absence of filling from progressively greater filling and incorporates stasis evaluation.

name: Kamran-Byrne Scale
description: The Kamran-Byrne (KB) Scale assesses both: (I) the degree of aneurysm occlusion using a five-point numerical scale [0 = no change, 1 = residual filling >50% of pretreatment aneurysm, 2 = residual filling <50% of aneurysm, 3 = residual filling confined to aneurysm neck, 4 = no residual filling or complete obliteration]; and (II) the patency status of the parent artery using a three-point scale [no change in parent artery diameter, narrowing of parent artery, or parent artery occlusion]. In total, there are 15 different grading possibilities.
description_reference: Mazur MD, Taussky, P, Shah, LD, et al. Inter-Rater Reliability of Published Flow Diversion Occlusion Scales. Journal of Neurointerventional Surgery 2016; 8: 1294–98. https://doi.org/10.1136/neurintsurg-2015-012193
domain_match_overall_rationale: The Kamran-Byrne (KB) Scale clasifies residual aneurysm filling after flow diversion treatment from no change in flow through to complete obliteration. The main domain match limitation is its specificity to flow diversion treatment.
domain_match_1_rationale: Assesses residual aneurysm filling after flow diversion treatment, including complete obliteration, partial filling, and no change in flow.
domain_match_3_rationale: Primarily evaluates degree of aneurysm occlusion. Also includes information on the patency status of parent artery.
domain_match_4_rationale: Defines categories of degree of aneurysm occlusion and patency status of parent artery, to assign an overall grade.
domain_match_6_rationale: Ordered categories from no change in flow through to complete obliteration.

name: Simple Measurement of Aneurysm Residual after Treatment
description_reference: Grunwald IQ, Kamran M, Corkill RA, et al. Simple Measurement of Aneurysm Residual after Treatment: The SMART Scale for Evaluation of Intracranial Aneurysms Treated with Flow Diverters. Acta Neurochirurgica 2012; 154: 21–26. https://doi.org/10.1007/s00701-011-1177-0
image: images/Simple Measurement of Aneurysm Residual after Treatment (SMART) Scale.png
domain_match_overall_rationale: The SMART-scale consists of a five-point grading scale that assesses residual flow within the aneurysm after treatment with a flow diverter.The SMART scale was explicitly created because coil-based scales were considered unsuitable for flow diversion; likewise, the SMART scale is not suitable for other treatment modalities.
domain_match_1_rationale: The SMART-scale consists of a five-point grading scale that assesses residual flow within the aneurysm after treatment with a flow diverter.
domain_match_3_rationale: Assesses residual flow within the aneurysm.
domain_match_5_rationale: Assesses residual flow within the aneurysm after treatment with a flow diverter.
domain_match_6_rationale: The SMART-scale classifies residual flow within the aneurysm, after treatment with a flow diverter, using a clearly defined five-point grading scale.

name: Remnant / residual aneurysm scales
description:
3D-DSA Remnant Scale: Uses three-dimensional digital subtraction angiography (3D-DSA) imaging to score postoperative aneurysm remnant size [0 = complete occlusion, 1 = remnant size < 2 mm, 2 = remnant size 2 to 4 mm, and 3 = remnant size > 4 mm"].

Kotowski 4-category postclipping remnant scale: 4-point scale [0 represents a complete aneurysm occlusion; 1 represents a small neck remnant (<2 mm and <50% of initial aneurysm size); 2 represents a remnant >=2 mm and <50% of initial aneurysm size; and 3 represents a remnant >=50% of the initial aneurysm size.

Dichotomized postclipping remnant scale: Dichotomization of the Kotowski categories (0/1 vs. 2/3), representing satisfactory and unsatisfactory angiographic results.
description_reference:
Halter M, Wanderer S, Grüter B, et al. Interrater and Intrarater Agreement Superior for Three-Dimensional Digital Subtraction Angiography (3D-DSA) over 2D-DSA Classification for Detecting Remnants after Intracranial Aneurysm Clipping, a GRRAS Reliability and Agreement Study. Acta Neurochirurgica 2022; 164: 2173–79. https://doi.org/10.1007/s00701-022-05156-3

Kotowski M, Farzin B, Fahed R, et al. Residual Cerebral Aneurysms After Microsurgical Clipping: A New Scale, an Agreement Study, and a Systematic Review of the Literature. World Neurosurgery 2019; 121: 302–21. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.wneu.2018.09.100

name: Sindou Classification
description: Sindou Classification uses three-dimensional digital subtraction angiography (3D-DSA) imaging to classify aneurysm remnants into two groups: N-group = with only a neck remnant; N-S group = with a residuum of neck and sac.
description_reference: Han MH and Kim YD. Role of Multislice Computerized Tomographic Angiography after Clip Placement in Aneurysm Patients Based on Comparison with Three Dimensional Digital Subtraction Angiography. Journal of Korean Neurosurgical Society 2007; 42: 103–11.
domain_match_1_rationale: Describes the amount and configuration of residual aneurysm after microsurgical clipping.
domain_match_3_rationale: Specifically classifies aneurysm remnants into two groups: N-group = with only a neck remnant; N-S group = with a residuum of neck and sac.
domain_match_4_rationale: Grades are based on the extent and morphology of the residual neck/sac.
domain_match_5_rationale: Can be applied post-operation and at follow-up.
domain_match_6_rationale: Clearly classifies aneurysm remnants into two groups: N-group = with only a neck remnant; N-S group = with a residuum of neck and sac.

name: Recurrence classification
description:
Dichotomous major recurrence scale: Presence/absence of a major cerebral aneurysm recurrence. 

Minor/major recurrence classification: Assessment of “no recurrence”, “minor recurrence”, or “major recurrence”. A recurrence was defined as “any increase in size of the remnant”. A recurrence was considered “major” if it would theoretically permit re-treatment with coils or “minor” if it did not cross this threshold.
description_reference:
Tollard É, Darsaut TE, Bing F, et al. Outcomes of Endovascular Treatments of Aneurysms: Observer Variability and Implications for Interpreting Case Series and Planning Randomized Trials. American Journal of Neuroradiology, 2012; 33: 626–31. https://doi.org/10.3174/ajnr.A2848 

Cloft HJ and Kallmes DF. Observer agreement in the assessment of minor and major cerebral aneurysm recurrence. Interventional neuroradiology 2011; 17: 411-4. https://doi.org/10.1177/159101991101700402

name: Computerized / software-based occlusion assessment
description:
Computerized Occlusion Rating (COR): an objective, software-based method designed to calculate the precise percentage of an intracranial aneurysm that has been successfully blocked off (occluded) after endovascular coil embolization.

Aneurysm recurrence volumetry: A volume of interest, with the aneurysm neck as the centre, is first mapped using a computer model. This computer model is then used estimate any changes in aneurysm volume after treatment.
description_reference:
Sherif C, Gruber A, Shuster E, et al. Computerized occlusion rating: a superior predictor of aneurysm rebleeding for ruptured embolized aneurysms. American journal of neuroradiology 2012; 33: 1481-7. https://doi.org/10.3174/ajnr.A3085

Schönfeld MH, Schlotfeldt V, Forkert ND, et al. Aneurysm Recurrence Volumetry Is More Sensitive than Visual Evaluation of Aneurysm Recurrences. Clinical Neuroradiology 2016; 26: 57–64. https://doi.org/10.1007/s00062-014-0330-6

name: CT angiography
description: Computed tomographic angiography (CTA): an imaging method used for the evaluation of both preoperative and post-clipped cerebral aneurysms.
description_reference: Kim HJ, Yoon DY, Kim ES, et al. 256-Row Multislice CT Angiography in the Postoperative Evaluation of Cerebral Aneurysms Treated with Titanium Clips: Using Three-Dimensional Rotational Angiography as the Standard of Reference. European Radiology 2020; 30: 2152–60. https://doi.org/10.1007/s00330-019-06560-7
domain_match_overall_rationale: CTA is an imaging technique that can be used to visualize  whether contrast continues to enter a treated aneurysm and can therefore help identify complete or incomplete obliteration; However, compared to available alternatives, CTA  is less sensitive. Similarly to other imaging techniques, it also does not itself prescribe an occlusion classification.
domain_match_1_rationale: Directly visualizes whether contrast continues to enter a treated aneurysm and can therefore help identify complete or incomplete obliteration.
domain_match_2_rationale: Can assess treated aneurysms and the surrounding vasculature, but small remnants and some treatment-device artifacts can reduce sensitivity.
domain_match_3_rationale: Visible residual filling, or lack thereof, can indicate degree of occlusion, but artifacts, such as from the treatment devices, create diagnostic uncertainty.
domain_match_4_rationale: CTA is a well-established imaging technique with clear interpretive guidance.
domain_match_5_rationale: Can assess occlusion post-treatment and at follow up.
domain_match_6_rationale: Can support occlusion classifications, but CTA itself does not prescribe a scoring system.

name: Digital subtraction angiography
description: Digital Subtraction Angiography (DSA) uses X-rays and contrast dye to visualize blood vessels, while a computer digitally removes bones from the image. It is used to see whether blood is still entering the treated aneurysm
description_reference: Glick Y, Balasubramanian S, Zheng A, et al. Digital subtraction angiography. Reference article, Radiopaedia.org. Available online: https://doi.org/10.53347/rID-62028 (Accessed on 17 Jun 2026)
domain_match_overall_rationale: DSA is a highly sensitive imaging technique that can be used to visualize  whether contrast continues to enter a treated aneurysm and can therefore help identify complete or incomplete obliteration; However, it does not itself prescribe an occlusion classification.
domain_match_1_rationale: Directly visualizes whether blood/contrast continues to circulate within the treated aneurysm.
domain_match_2_rationale: Excellent  resolution allows for assessment of complete occlusion, tiny remnants, and complex aneurysm geometry across multiple treatment techniques.
domain_match_3_rationale: Provides highly sensitive imaging of residual filling, or lack thereof, which can be used to assess the degree of occlusion.
domain_match_4_rationale: DSA is a standardized angiographic technique and remains the reference standard against which other imaging techniques are commonly compared.
domain_match_5_rationale: Can assess occlusion immediately following procedure and at follow up.
domain_match_6_rationale: Can support occlusion classifications, but DSA itself does not prescribe a scoring system.

name: Magnetic resonance angiography
description: Magnetic resonance angiography (MRA) is a type of magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) that looks specifically at blood vessels. It is used to check whether blood is still flowing into the aneurysm after treatment.
description_reference: John Hopkins Medicine. Magnetic Resonance Angiography (MRA). The Johns Hopkins University, The Johns Hopkins Hospital, and Johns Hopkins Health System. Available online: https://www.hopkinsmedicine.org/health/treatment-tests-and-therapies/magnetic-resonance-angiography-mra (Accessed on 17 Jun 2026)

name: Intraoperative assessment techniques
description:
Intraoperative microvascular Doppler (IMD) is a technique used to assist in correct aneurysm clip placement.

Indocyanine green (ICG) videoangiography is a quick, reliable, cost-effective method for assessing flow in large and small vessels that are visible with the operating microscope.
description_reference:
Hui P, Yan Y, Zhang S, et al. Intraoperative Microvascular Doppler Monitoring in Intracranial Aneurysm Surgery. Chinese Medical Journal 2013; 126: 2424–29. https://doi.org/10.3760/cma.j.issn.0366-6999.20130395

Raabe A, Beck J, Gerlach R, et al. (2003). Near-infrared Indocyanine Green Video Angiography: A New Method for Intraoperative Assessment of Vascular Flow. Neurosurgery 2003 52: 132-139. https://doi.org/10.1097/00006123-200301000-00017
